title: Klaviyo MCP server
snippet:
Configure Klaviyo's MCP server to get AI assistance with your Klaviyo data.
##
You will learn
The Klaviyo Model Context Protocol (MCP) server seamlessly integrates with Klaviyo’s APIs, enabling AI clients to interact with your Klaviyo data. This guide will walk you through configuring various MCP clients for both the remote-hosted MCP server (recommended) and the local MCP server.
##
What is MCP?
[MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction) (Model Context Protocol) is an open protocol that helps AI models securely interface with different data sources and tools. You’ll connect Klaviyo’s MCP server to an MCP client, i.e., an AI agent like Claude or Cursor, to get assistance with your Klaviyo data. Your MCP client can help with a [variety of tasks](/en/docs/klaviyo_mcp_server#available-tools) from campaign creation to flow performance reports. Here’s some examples of prompts you can give:
- “Show me the performance of my email campaigns from the last 30 days.”
- “Which flows are performing the best in terms of conversions?”
- “Create an email campaign promoting our Memorial Day sale.”

##
Configure your MCP client for the remote-hosted server (recommended)
> ##
>
> This feature is only available to Klaviyo users with an Owner, Admin, or Manager role. Learn more about [Klaviyo user roles](https://help.klaviyo.com/hc/en-us/articles/115005231648).
> ##
>
> By default, the remote-hosted server includes many tools. If your client has a smaller context window or you want to improve tool-selection accuracy, add the `core-tools-only=true` query parameter to limit the server to the ~40 core tools (see [*Query parameters*](/en/docs/klaviyo_mcp_server#query-parameters)).
To communicate with the Klaviyo MCP server, each MCP client needs specific configuration. Follow the steps below to get started:
1. Log in to the Klaviyo account you'd like to use.
2. Follow the steps below for the MCP client you’d like to configure.
###
Claude
####
Listed Connector (recommended for connecting to a single Klaviyo account)
The listed Klaviyo connector is the simplest way to access Klaviyo within Claude.
1. In Claude, navigate to [Settings > Connectors](https://claude.ai/settings/connectors).
2. Click **Browse Connectors**.
3. Search for **Klaviyo** and connect.
4. Review the Claude access and click **Approve**.
5. Review the permissions for your Klaviyo account and click **Allow**.
You're now ready to ask Claude about your Klaviyo data.

title: Klaviyo MCP Server Guide For Agencies | Klaviyo Help Center
snippet:
The Klaviyo MCP (Model Context Protocol) server is a secure bridge that lets AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT connect directly to Klaviyo. Once connected, you can talk to your Klaviyo account in plain language: ask questions, pull reports, analyze performance, and draft or create campaigns and templates, without logging into the dashboard and exporting data by hand.
Under the hood it is a wrapper on top of Klaviyo's APIs. You authorize each account separately, and the AI assistant can then read that account's data and take supported actions within the permissions you grant.

To connect an account you will need:
- **An Owner, Admin, or Manager role** on each Klaviyo account you want to connect.
- **A Claude or ChatGPT account.** Connecting several accounts (custom connector) requires a paid Claude plan (Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise) or ChatGPT developer mode. *This guide covers Claude setup.*
- For Claude Team or Enterprise, someone with permission to add custom connectors must first add the connector to your organization. Members then connect it to their own Klaviyo accounts. See [Claude’s custom connector setup instructions](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-getting-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp).
- **The remote MCP server URL:** https://mcp.klaviyo.com/mcp
## **Step 1: Connect multiple client accounts**
Use a custom connector for each client account you manage. The steps below describe setup on Claude Pro or Max. For Team or Enterprise, follow [Claude’s organization setup instructions](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-getting-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp), using the account name and URL in steps 3 and 4, then complete Klaviyo authorization in step 6. Repeat the setup for every account.
**1. In Claude, open the Connectors area**
- In the web browser or desktop app, go to **Customize**.
- Select **Connectors**.
- This is where you manage and add integrations.

Enter the connector URL**
- Enter [https://mcp.klaviyo.com/mcp?company=example-company](https://mcp.klaviyo.com/mcp?company=example-company). Replace `example-company` with the client account name, using `%20` for spaces.
- The company name in the URL helps distinguish connectors.

To prevent the connector from changing Klaviyo data, add `&read-only=true` to its account-specific URL, for example `https://mcp.klaviyo.com/mcp?company=example-company&read-only=true`. This hides and blocks tools that write or delete data.

title: Klaviyo MCP Server: Analyze Performance & Build Campaigns With AI - Klaviyo
snippet:
The Klaviyo MCP server connects compatible AI clients to Klaviyo APIs through an authorized Model Context Protocol connection. It supports permitted reporting and account actions, with configurable tools, scopes, and access controls.
- **Plain-language tasks:** Compatible AI clients can retrieve campaign results, compare flow performance, or create campaigns when supported.
- **Flexible client support:** Documented connection options include Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, and other compatible remote MCP clients.
---
## What is the Klaviyo MCP server?
The Klaviyo MCP server connects compatible AI clients to Klaviyo APIs through Model Context Protocol (MCP). MCP is an open protocol that helps AI models securely interface with data sources and tools.
The server gives an AI client a defined set of Klaviyo tools. Depending on the tools and permissions available, you can ask the client to retrieve campaign results, compare flow performance, or create a campaign.
### Why the Klaviyo MCP server matters
An AI client needs an authorized connection before it can work with data or tools in your Klaviyo account. The Klaviyo MCP server provides that connection, so the client can handle supported requests based on the access you approve.
A few of the benefits:
- Account context: The client can request authorized Klaviyo information as part of a task.
- Analysis and action: Available tools support performance reporting and permitted account actions.
- Client choice: You can connect Klaviyo to a compatible AI client that fits how your team works.
## Why choose the Klaviyo MCP server
The Klaviyo MCP server integrates with Klaviyo APIs and exposes supported tools to your AI client. Klaviyo recommends the remote-hosted server for connecting an MCP client.
### Work in the AI client you already use
Klaviyo documents connection options for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and VS Code. You can also connect another MCP client that supports remote servers, OAuth with dynamic client registration, and Streamable HTTP.
### Move between performance questions and marketing tasks
The Klaviyo MCP server offers tools across campaigns, flows, profiles, reporting, catalogs, events, and other documented categories. You can ask for email campaign performance over a set period, compare flows by conversions, or create an email campaign. The client can complete only requests supported by its available tools and permissions.
